thread:
james (Customer): Hey team — after our IdP cert rotation this morning, our users are seeing SSO failures during login. Getting 'Invalid SAML Response' and some 'ACS URL mismatch' messages in the SP logs. Started ~08:15 UTC. Can you help? :grimacing:

maria (Support): Sorry about that, james. Can you paste the exact error the SP (your side) is seeing and the time for a repro attempt? Also, did you upload new IdP metadata to our console or only rotate on the IdP side?

james (Customer): Error from our side (raw):
```
[2026-03-27T08:17:42Z] saml: Assertion Consumer Service URL mismatch: expected https://app.redwood.ai/sso/saml/acs, got https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs
[2026-03-27T08:17:42Z] saml: Signature verification failed: X509 Certificate expired
```
We rotated certs in Okta this morning and pushed metadata. Not sure if we updated the EntityID/ACS fields — they should be same as before.

maria (Support): Thanks. Two parallel checks: (1) our SP (Redwood) expects a specific ACS URL and EntityID based on the customer's SP config in Console; if the IdP sends a different ACS in the SAMLRequest/Response it can be rejected. (2) Signature errors point to an expired cert in the SAMLResponse. Could you confirm the full IdP metadata XML you uploaded to Redwood or paste the IdP metadata URL?

james (Customer): We uploaded metadata.xml exported from Okta at 07:50 UTC. Here's the metadata URL we used (internal): https://idp.company.com/metadata.xml

maria (Support): Got it. I'm going to escalate to Identity infra for a quick metadata/EntityID check. @anna can you validate whether the SP record for customer 'acme-corp' on Redwood side still has the old ACS or a different EntityID? Also check if our console applied the new signing cert or if it still points to the old (expired) cert.

anna (Identity): Pulling logs... idp-monitor-bot shows an automatic metadata fetch ran at 07:52 and succeeded, but the metadata contains two <AssertionConsumerService> entries. The primary one in metadata says https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs (legacy), and there's another with index=1 set to https://app.redwood.ai/sso/saml/acs (current). The SP config in our DB is set to the latter (https://app.redwood.ai/sso/saml/acs) so when the IdP sends the legacy ACS it fails with 'ACS URL mismatch'.

anna (Identity): Also the IdP's signing cert in the uploaded metadata expires 2026-03-27T07:45:00Z — so indeed the cert used to sign the SAMLResponse may be the old one and signature validation will fail once clocks pass expiry. There's a race when Okta rotates where some nodes still sign with old cert for a short window.

maria (Support): Good findings. Two actionable items for customer: 1) Adjust the IdP so that the default ACS it uses (the one bound to the Okta App) matches our configured SP ACS (https://app.redwood.ai/sso/saml/acs). 2) Re-trigger a login after 5 minutes; signature failures should stop once Okta signs with the new cert. In parallel we'll temporarily accept the legacy ACS to help the cutover.

tom (SRE): Heads-up — changing SP validation rules has risk. If we relax ACS strictness we could accept a malicious redirect if EntityID/Audience not checked. Before any change we should ensure AudienceRestriction and EntityID still match and only allow alternate ACS when EntityID is exact match.

maria (Support): Agreed. @anna can you create a short-lived tolerant rule for the acme-corp tenant: accept ACS https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs only if Response/Assertion Audience==urn:redwood:sp:acme-corp and Issuer matches the IdP entityID from their metadata? Limit to 60 minutes and log all occurrences.

anna (Identity): Done. Rule deployed to canary for acme-corp at 08:29 UTC with a 60-minute TTL. Logging enabled.

maria (Support): james — can you try a login now and paste the new SAML debug output (SAMLResponse status / signature error if any)? If you can't, use SAML-tracer or browser extension and paste the SAMLResponse (or at least the Response/Issuer and Assertion/Subject/NameID).

james (Customer): Retried at 08:31. New log shows:
```
[2026-03-27T08:31:10Z] saml: Response accepted (alternate ACS allowed). Audience OK. Issuer: https://idp.company.com
[2026-03-27T08:31:10Z] saml: Signature verification OK (using new cert)
```
Users are able to log in again. Thanks.

maria (Support): Great. We'll keep the tolerant rule active until 09:29 UTC and monitor. @tom can we add an alert if tolerant-rule acceptance rate > 1% for that tenant (to catch misconfigurations)?

tom (SRE): Yep, creating a Prometheus rule to alert when tolerant-acs-accepts{tenant="acme-corp"} > 0.01 for 5m. Will also add a grafana panel.

anna (Identity): Follow-up: I pulled the exact metadata from the IdP at 07:52 and it's here (redacted):
```
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.company.com" xmlns="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:metadata">
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <KeyInfo><X509Data><X509Certificate>MIID...OLD_CERT...==</X509Certificate></X509Data></KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
    <SingleSignOnService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-Redirect" Location="https://idp.company.com/sso/redirect"/>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
  <AssertionConsumerService index="0" isDefault="true" Location="https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs"/>
  <AssertionConsumerService index="1" Location="https://app.redwood.ai/sso/saml/acs"/>
</EntityDescriptor>
```
Note: Old cert expiry 2026-03-27T07:45, new cert present in metadata at index next fetch (07:56).

maria (Support): james — recommended permanent fixes: 1) Ensure the Okta app's ACS URL is the canonical one we expect: https://app.redwood.ai/sso/saml/acs (we can accept the legacy temporarily but canonicalization prevents future breakage). 2) Configure Okta to publish new metadata and double-check rotation windows (Okta docs suggest overlapping certs for 48h to avoid this). 3) If you want us to, we can accept both ACS entries permanently for a short period, but that's not recommended.

james (Customer): We'll update the Okta app to set the single ACS as https://app.redwood.ai/sso/saml/acs and verify rotation policy. Can you confirm logs after 09:00 that no tolerant-rule hits happened?

maria (Support): Affirmative — we'll monitor and post a final update.

tom (SRE): Alert rule created and test fired a sample metric at 08:34 during the repro. I'll post a screenshot to the ticket.

anna (Identity): Quick note for runbook: Reason for these transient failures = IdP metadata contained multiple ACS entries and some IdP nodes signed responses with the old key during rotation. Remediation path: (a) canonicalize ACS in IdP app, (b) ensure metadata uploaded to Redwood Console, (c) ensure cert overlap or push new metadata early, (d) if immediate cutover needed, request temporary tolerant acceptance from Redwood identity team.

maria (Support): Closing the loop — tolerant rule expired at 09:29 with zero further accepts after 08:40. All clear on our side. james, if you want the ticket closed after you confirm your Okta change, ping me and we'll close. :white_check_mark:

james (Customer): Confirmed — Okta app updated at 09:05, users reporting nominal logins. Thanks everyone for the quick triage and the temporary fix.

maria (Support): Thanks team! Filing a short internal postmortem note to eng-security about improving guidance for customers doing IdP rotations (include recommended metadata/ACS checks).

idp-monitor-bot: automated fetch of https://idp.company.com/metadata.xml at 07:52 succeeded (sha256=abc123), fetch at 07:56 succeeded (sha256=def456).

maria (Support): Postmortem summary (for internal channel): Root cause: IdP rotation with multiple ACS entries + old cert signing within rotation window. Mitigation: temporary tolerant-ACS rule for affected tenant; customer canonicalized ACS and confirmed new cert in metadata. Action items: doc update, add dashboard/alert, consider optional console helper to validate IdP metadata before import.
